draft.title: Are bamboo toothbrushes actually better
draft.metaDescription: What a bamboo handle changes, and what it does not.
draft.intro: The handle composts and the bristles do not, which is the whole answer. Bamboo Soft has a moso bamboo handle that is home compostable once the nylon-6 bristles are pulled out — a step most people will not take, and without it the brush goes in the bin like any other.

sections.heading: What is actually different
sections.body: Bamboo Soft is an FSC-certified bamboo handle with nylon-6 bristles at 12 g. Recycled Soft is a recycled polypropylene handle with the same nylon-6 bristles at 18 g. The bristles are identical; only the handle differs, and the handle is roughly two thirds of the object by weight.

sections.heading: The honest comparison
sections.body: If you will remove the bristles, bamboo wins on disposal. If you will not, a recycled-plastic handle that is already made from waste plastic and goes in the dishwasher is arguably the better choice. Neither of those is a marketing answer; it depends on a step you either take or do not.

sections.heading: Care, which is where bamboo asks more of you
sections.body: Bamboo Soft has to dry between uses or the handle will swell. Recycled Soft is dishwasher safe. That is a real difference in a shared bathroom.

factSheet.care: dry between uses; handle is home compostable once bristles are removed

competitorAngles.excerpt: The handle composts; the bristles do not.

note: Refuses the easy answer and names the condition the decision actually rests on.
